name: select_build_offer
prompt: Build me a playbook that runs when an alert is created, looks up the alert's source IP in VirusTotal, and sets the alert severity to High when the IP is malicious. Save it when it's ready.

forbidden_facts.label: researched step types instead of delivering
researched op schemas instead of delivering

notes: The build-path failure, now three observed shapes. (1) research-then-prose: it looks up step types and connectors and narrates what it would build. (2) verify-then-prose: verify_playbook passes, then it narrates instead of offering -- or, on a slower model, spends the whole turn budget and returns no final text at all, holding a playbook that is ready_to_push. (3) push-instead-of-offer: it calls push_playbook directly and then tells the analyst to click a Deploy button that does not exist. Shape 3 is worse than the other two, not a milder version of them -- it is an ungated state-changing write plus a hallucinated affordance, so P2 gating is what fails, not just delivery. Either way the analyst gets no offer, so the terminal tool is emit_playbook_offer, not verify_playbook or push_playbook. Decoys here are legitimate preparatory calls -- they are recorded to show what the offer is losing to, and never fail the gate on their own.
